title: Audit Chronicle: region-aware sealing and automated evidence shipping for admin actions
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Scope: build a reliable pipeline that captures admin actions, access events, and configuration changes; persisting tamper-evident evidence with region-residency guarantees and configurable retention. The feature must produce verifiable artifacts suitable for legal/regulatory audits and integrate with Redwood Private and Dedicated deployments. Goals: 1) Ensure audit events are sealed into tamper-evident archives immediately after commit. 2) Enforce per-customer residency and retention policies during archiving. 3) Provide automated export hooks and proofs for auditors (hash manifests, HSM stamps). 4) Minimize runtime impact on API latency and maintainability. Out of scope: full search UX for auditors (handled by separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Audit events (admin action, access, config change) are written to a write-once staging ledger within 5s of occurrence for >=95% of events
A sealed archive manifest (SHA256 per-segment + manifest root) is generated and anchored to HSM or KMS-backed signing key within the same retention zone
Archives respect customer residency tag (e.g., eu-west-1, us-east-1) and never leave allowed regions during sealing and storage
Retention lifecycle (retention TTL, legal hold) applied automatically; deletion requests for sealed evidence are rejected when legal hold is present
An automated evidence-export job can produce a time-bounded export with integrity proofs for auditors and emits an audit_export job record
Operational dashboards surface backlog of unsealed segments, seal latency percentiles, and per-customer residency violations (zero tolerated)
Unit and integration tests cover sealing logic, residency routing, and export proof validation
implementation_notes: Event flow: API -> kafka topic (region-tagged) -> write-once segmenter -> async sealer -> immutable object store (WORM-enabled)
Use prefix-based KV cache to batch small admin events into append-only segments to optimize sealing frequency and object count
Sealer will compute per-segment SHA256 tree and produce a manifest that is signed with KMS/HSM key. Use HSM stamping for enterprise private deployments where available
Retention controller will be policy-driven (customer profile stores residency and retention windows) and must surface legal hold flags from customer tenant service
For Dedicated/Private, allow configuring a local HSM endpoint and local object store endpoints; fallback to Redwood hosted signatures only if customer consents

Design trade-off: sealing every event provides strongest integrity but high object churn. We choose a 30s or 10k-event segment trigger (configurable per-customer) to balance cost and forensic granularity
Seal operation must be idempotent and resumable; use sequence numbers and tombstones to avoid double-archiving
Retention immutability: leverage storage class with object immutability flags where available (S3 Object Lock / WORM) and fall back to cryptographic proofs if not supported
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dogfood): enable for internal org and security team tenants only; validate sealer correctness and proof verification; 2-week monitoring window
Phase 2 (opt-in): invite select customers with compliance needs to opt-in; collect feedback and tune segment sizing and sign latency
Phase 3 (default-on for enterprise): enable by default for Dedicated and Private customers with per-tenant policy pages in Console for residency and retention settings
Fallbacks: provide read-only access to unsealed staging for diagnostic only in dogfood; never expose staging data to customers in general rollout
Communications: update Trust & Compliance docs, generate runbook for legal export requests, and publish integration guide for HSM/KMS and object store configuration
